scope: Layer 1: tokens and themes (T1-T6) for web: packages/styles (foundation, semantics, personalization axes, the four themes), the Tailwind and shadcn bridges, and Figma parity. Swift/iOS parity is out of scope this round (iOS backlog).

scores.evidence: At the root every theme x mode x brand combination resolves: contrast.browser.test.ts:146-178 and :231-292 pass, and figma-parity.browser.test.ts:145-189 compares every theme x brand x surface x mode color. Gap: --a63-status-{info,success,warning,danger}-foreground are declared only in the light block (semantics.css:234-264) and read var(--a63-status-*) there, while the dark block (semantics.css:404-415) re-declares status-* and status-*-subtle but not -foreground. Inside a nested [data-a63-mode='dark'] scope under a light root (UIProvider mode="dark", provider.tsx:72) the foreground stays computed from step 600, so info-500 and danger-500 fills get near-white text. The nested-scope contrast test (contrast.browser.test.ts:184-208) does not list this pair.

Declared pairs pass on every theme, mode and brand (contrast.browser.test.ts:12-57, :212-229; sweep build log is green). Pairs that are not declared and fail: (a) near-white text on a nested dark info-500 fill is 3.39:1 and on danger-500 3.85:1 (computed from primitives.css:94,105; L_oklab 0.634/0.622, see T1); (b) --a63-chart-2 (teal-500) is about 2.3:1 and --a63-chart-3 (amber-500) about 2.0:1 against the light page (semantics.css:270-271; palette.css:43,98 vs n1-light-2 rgb(249,249,249)), under WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 for chart marks; (c) the craft baseline carries 6 token-role entries where --a63-text-primary paints a fill and --a63-surface-page paints text (craft-baseline.json: card.css, input-otp.css, slider.css, kbd.css, mdx timeline.css), so the system has no inverse-surface token for that role.

Grammar is mostly one family (--a63-<group>-<role>[-state]), but: (1) dead tokens are not checked. check-token-economy.mjs:42-46 only looks for unused tokens with the --theme-/--gel- prefixes, and `grep -rhoE '^\s*--(theme|gel)-' packages/styles/src | wc -l` is 0, so the advisory always reports 0. A multiline-aware scan of packages/ and apps/ finds 60 --a63-* tokens declared in packages/styles/src that nothing reads, e.g. 40 --a63-badge-<hue>-accent/-foreground (contracts/badge.css:10-53, badge.css reads --badge-bg instead), --a63-status-danger-subtle(-foreground) (semantics.css:265-266), --a63-choice-thumb, --a63-toggle-group-gap, --a63-toggle-shadow-active, --a63-weather-border-color/-divider-color/-muted-foreground/-text-shadow (set by three themes, read by no web recipe). (2) Component-tier tokens live in the semantic layer (--a63-alert-background, --a63-choice-card-checked-*, --a63-control-outline-* in semantics.css:187-205). (3) --a63-surface-sidebar and --a63-surface-recessed are the same value in both modes (semantics.css:142-144, 345-346).

Radius is one linear multiplier ramp (foundation/radius.css:16-37) and density scales space and control heights by one unit (density.browser.test.ts:41-56). The type scale is not monotonic: --typography-10xl-font-size is a fixed 40px (foundation/typography.css:47) while 9xl becomes 44px at 640px and 49px at 768px (typography.css:53-98), so the display role (type-roles.css:27) is smaller than the 9xl step on tablet and desktop. At the base width 9xl to 10xl is a 1px step (39 to 40) and 10xl to 11xl is a 1.4x jump (40 to 56). Body-range steps are uneven (13 to 15 to 16 to 18 to 19). Stale doc comment: radius.css:29 says --radius-full is 2x md, but the value at :32 is 2x xl.

CSS and Figma agree on every synced variable: figma-parity.browser.test.ts compares every mode of every axis and every theme x brand x surface x mode color; `pnpm -s run check:figma` -> 'Figma sync model is current.'; `check:dtcg`, `check:tokens` current. Swift side n/a this round (iOS backlog). Not 4: 64 'computed' variables (including --a63-text-primary, --a63-surface-page, --a63-border-*) are excluded from the comparison and show Figma their default only (atom63.figma-sync.json summary).
n/a: scored under the 'Personalization axes' (brand) and 'Theme authoring' subjects.

subjects.subject: Personalization axes (brand, surface, surface tint, radius, type scale, density, font, mode)

scores.evidence: Axes resolve on <html> but not on a nested scope, which personalization-axes.md:4 promises ('applied at any scope and inherited'). UIProvider stamps a dimension alone (provider.tsx:68 brand, :73 surface, :74 theme). brand-action.css:14-15 re-declares --a63-action-primary on [data-a63-brand], but --a63-text-accent (semantics.css:161,360), --a63-focus-ring (:209,395), --a63-selected-accent-background (:301,445), --a63-choice-card-checked-* (:199-205,388-393) and every tinted surface and border (:100-185) are declared only on :root/.light/.dark/[data-a63-mode]. So <UIProvider brand="b3"> paints the button b3-700 while links, the focus ring and the accent selection stay b1. The same holds for surface: surface.css:9-10 remaps --surface-light-* on [data-a63-surface], but the semantic surfaces read them on the mode scope. personalization-axes.md:71 says --a63-focus-ring is in brand.css scoped to [data-a63-brand], which is not true. Radius and type scale do nothing on a nested scope: the --radius-* ramp (foundation/radius.css:16-32) and --typography-* (typography.css:18-49) are declared at :root, and radius.css:14 and type-scale.css:9-10 claim a subtree can override. story-probes.tsx:108-131 confirms ('it FREEZES to the root multiplier') and works around it by re-emitting the ramp inline. The test helpers set every axis on documentElement only (test/apply-styles.ts:6-8). Density alone is done right and tested on a nested scope (density.browser.test.ts:75-86). mode='system' on UIProvider stamps light regardless of the OS preference (provider.tsx:65).

Six brands x four themes x two modes pass the primary fill/foreground, brand text, focus ring (3:1 on page, panel and field) and input border pairs (contrast.browser.test.ts:211-255), plus the neutral and accent selections (:257-292). Per-brand contrast exceptions are documented in brand-action.css:41-65.

Attributes follow data-a63-<axis> (personalization-axes.md:19-33). Legacy duplicates remain and are tested as aliases: [data-density] and [data-input] beside data-a63-* (token-economy.log: ':is([data-a63-density], [data-density])', ':is([data-a63-input='touch'], [data-input='touch'])'; density.browser.test.ts:77-78), and the .dark/.light classes beside data-a63-mode.

Radius multipliers 0/0.5/1/1.5 and type-scale 0.9/1/1.1/1.2 are tested (personalization-axes.browser.test.ts:13-24, 88-101). Compact density is a single 0.875 unit applied once to space, control heights, paddings and gaps (density.browser.test.ts:41-56). The density axis does not reach Tailwind spacing utilities (see the Tailwind bridge subject).

Figma has one collection per axis with matching modes: Brand 6, Surface 6, Density 2, Radius 4, Type Scale 4, Font 4, Input 3, Design Language 2, Window Size 3 (node read of generated/atom63.figma-sync.json), compared by figma-parity.browser.test.ts:139-147. The 'auto' brand (11 tokens) is skipped by design (runtime wallpaper ramp).

Adding a brand is documented step by step (theme-authoring.md:79-117), and check-theme-authoring.mjs:55 (brandListProblems) fails while any of the hand-written brand lists disagrees with brand-ramp.resolver.json. Polish: eight hand-written lists still have to be edited (theme-authoring.md:96-104).

Contrast and Figma parity pass for modern in both modes, at the root and in a nested theme+mode scope (contrast.browser.test.ts:146-208). Polish: the dark rule [data-a63-theme='modern']:is(.dark,[data-a63-mode='dark']) (modern.css:47-51) has no descendant form, so a nested dark scope under a light modern root loses the darker widget face.

All declared pairs pass for modern/light and modern/dark (contrast.browser.test.ts:146-208). Baseline: apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-button-themes-chromium-linux.png shows legible primary, default, danger, outline and ghost labels in both modes.
Assigns contract hooks only (modern.css:16-45: control, field and segment hooks); no new token tree.
n/a: a theme owns no scale; radius, type and space come from the axes (theme-authoring.md:36).
Figma Theme collection modes modern-light/modern-dark (figma-sync Theme collection, 8 modes); figma-parity theme x mode contexts pass.
n/a: scored under the 'Theme authoring' subject.

The aqua page and panel tint and the dark menu highlight are keyed to the theme and the mode on the same element (aqua.css:112, :134). Unlike terminal.css:94,152, aqua has no descendant re-assertion. So (a) a nested <UIProvider mode="dark"> inside an aqua root re-runs the semantic dark block (semantics.css:306-326) and gets neutral modern-dark surfaces, and (b) <UIProvider theme="aqua"> under a root whose mode comes from the html class matches neither rule and stays untinted. The nested contrast test always stamps theme and mode together (contrast.browser.test.ts:189-191), so neither case is covered.
Declared pairs pass for aqua in both modes, at the root and nested (contrast.browser.test.ts:146-208), including brand text on the tinted page (brand-action.css:49-53 b2 exception).
Theme-private helper --aqua-overlay-drop (aqua.css:23) plus contract hooks; follows theme-authoring.md:38-45.
n/a: a theme owns no scale; aqua sets --a63-control-radius: var(--radius-md) from the shared ramp (aqua.css:26).

aqua-light and aqua-dark carry concrete surface values in the Figma Theme collection (e.g. --a63-surface-page aqua-light rgb 0.937/0.954/0.981); parity passes. Gel shadows are skipped as unsupported string types (by design).
n/a: scored under the 'Theme authoring' subject.
Retro is material-only (retro.css:13-108, one [data-a63-theme='retro'] block with no mode split), so it follows the semantic mode at any scope. Contrast and parity pass in both modes.
Declared pairs pass (contrast.browser.test.ts:146-208); ui-react-button-themes-chromium-linux.png retro/light and retro/dark show legible bevelled labels.
Theme-private --retro-bevel-drop* helpers (retro.css:15-18) and contract hooks only.
n/a: a theme owns no scale; the square corners come from the radius axis (retro.css:58-59 comment).

retro-light and retro-dark in the Figma Theme collection; parity passes. --a63-widget-rim-border-color (a four-color list) is kept at its default in Figma (figma-sync skipped: 'theme value not representable').
n/a: scored under the 'Theme authoring' subject.

The phosphor palette (text, borders, surfaces, neutral action) applies only when the mode sits on the theme element or a descendant (terminal.css:93-94, 151-152). <UIProvider theme="terminal"> under a root whose mode comes from the html class matches neither, so the CRT glow appears (terminal.css:27-91) over neutral modern text and surfaces. Phosphor text is a mix of --a63-action-primary computed on the theme element (terminal.css:96-99, 154-158), so a nested brand-only scope inside terminal keeps the root brand's text color. Neither case is tested.
Declared pairs pass in both modes for all six brands, including the reverse-video toggle pair (contrast.browser.test.ts:43-45; terminal.css:147-148, 183-184).
Theme-private --terminal-overlay-glow (terminal.css:29) plus contract hooks; the mode split is documented in the header (terminal.css:11-17).
n/a: a theme owns no scale; corners come from the radius axis (terminal.css:55-56).

Terminal text and surfaces track the brand (color-mix with --a63-action-primary, terminal.css:96-163), but Figma's Theme collection holds one value per theme-mode, and these tokens are in the model's 'computed' list (variesOn brand, mode, surface, theme; e.g. --a63-text-primary). Figma shows the b1 phosphor whatever Brand mode the designer picks, and the parity test leaves computed tokens out (figma-parity.browser.test.ts:15-19, :134).

The new-theme checklist (theme-authoring.md:58-75) names the resolver and the path in check-theme-authoring.mjs, which hard-codes the four themes (check-theme-authoring.mjs:15-21). Theme ids are also hand-listed in themes/index.css:1-4, ui-foundation/src/axes.ts, ui-react/src/theme/core/types.ts and options.ts, styles/scripts/generate-figma-sync.mjs, contrast.browser.test.ts:9, figma-parity.browser.test.ts:145,150 and story-probes THEME_RADIUS_SCALE (grep for 'terminal'). Brands have a drift check (brandListProblems); themes have none. A fifth theme missed in any one of these lists is skipped by the contrast and parity tests without a failure.

Every block is @theme inline (theme.css:4,309,344,478,488), so a utility emits var(--a63-*) at the element and follows nested scopes as far as the semantic layer does. Semantic roles are generated from roles.json (theme.css:343); `pnpm -s run check:roles` -> 'Role bridges are current.'

check:craft token-role reads roles.json, so `text-primary` (a fill) used as text is flagged in TSX (craft-rules.mjs:36-46; check-craft.mjs:80-88). It exposes text-info-foreground, text-success-foreground and text-warning-foreground (theme.css:366-370), which carry the nested-dark status-foreground issue from the semantic layer.

It reuses Tailwind's names with other values. text-6xl is 28px here, against 60px in Tailwind (typography.css:39; theme.css text block). The 10xl and 11xl steps that the display roles use are not exposed. rounded-full is a pill (theme.css:517-519), while the CSS variable --radius-full is a soft 28px corner (foundation/radius.css:32): one name, two meanings. `secondary` and `muted` map to the same token (roles.json).

theme.css defines no --spacing (grep 'spacing' in theme.css finds nothing), so p-*, gap-* and m-* use Tailwind's fixed 0.25rem unit and ignore [data-a63-density]. Templates lay out with these utilities (e.g. the app-view template's 'flex flex-col gap-6 p-6'), so compact density tightens the components but not the page rhythm around them.
n/a: the bridge re-exposes the CSS tokens; Figma parity is scored on the token subjects.
A role is added once in roles.json and generated into both bridges (generate-role-bridges.mjs; check:roles in CI). Brands and themes need no Tailwind edits because utilities read --a63-*.

shadcn.css declares its aliases on ':root, .light, .dark, [data-a63-mode]' only (shadcn.css:14-17). Inside <UIProvider brand="b3"> (no mode), --a63-action-primary is re-declared on the scope (brand-action.css:14-15), but --primary and --ring keep the root values, so shadcn components there use the wrong brand. The same applies to theme-only and surface-only scopes. a63-from-shadcn.css declares everything on :root only (a63-from-shadcn.css:15), so a nested .dark in a shadcn app keeps the root's light values.

a63-from-shadcn.css:40-45 hard-codes --a63-status-{info,success,warning}-foreground: white. With its own fallback --warning oklch(0.75 0.15 80), white text is about 2:1; with the success fallback oklch(0.65 0.16 150), it is under 3:1. No test covers the reverse bridge's pairs. A coverage scan finds only 4 --a63-* tokens read by ui-react CSS that the reverse bridge does not supply (--a63-grid-line-color, --a63-lightbox-aspect and --a63-type-body-font-size/-line-height, the last two in reset.css only).
Generated from roles.json with the verbatim shadcn names (shadcn.css:4-11). Polish: it adds global unprefixed --light and --dark (shadcn.css:166-167), which can collide with app variables.
n/a: the bridge holds colors only; no scale.
n/a: not mirrored to Figma by design.
shadcn.css is generated (check:roles); a new brand or theme needs no edit to either bridge.

14 collections and 1150 variables, with every axis as a collection of modes (summary in atom63.figma-sync.json); figma-parity.browser.test.ts resolves each variable the way Figma does and compares it with the browser on every mode of every axis.
n/a: contrast is scored on the web tokens, which Figma mirrors.
Figma paths follow the token names (`pnpm -s atom63 token --a63-focus-ring` -> 'Figma: Semantic / focus/ring').
n/a: scales are scored on the token subjects.

Parity holds for what is synced, but 279 tokens are skipped and 64 are approximated (model summary). The skips that a designer will notice: 60 phone form-factor tokens ("context scope: [data-a63-form-factor='phone']"), 32 density-scoped tokens such as compact control paddings and gaps, and 53 'conditional' (coarse-pointer target sizes, reduced motion). The computed list includes the control heights (--a63-control-height-xs..xl) and the terminal and brand-tinted text and surfaces. A designer who sets Density=compact or a phone frame in Figma sees comfortable, desktop control geometry.
A new brand mode means one hand edit to generate-figma-sync.mjs (theme-authoring.md:98-99), caught by check:theme-authoring; `pnpm -s run check:figma` -> current.

findings.subject: Personalization axes (brand, surface, surface tint, radius, type scale, density, font, mode)
findings.summary: On a nested scope, the brand and surface axes only half apply. <UIProvider brand=...> or <UIProvider surface=...> without a mode changes the primary fill but leaves links, the focus ring, the accent selection, the choice-card check and every surface, text and border token on the root's brand and neutrals.
findings.evidence: provider.tsx:68,73 stamp data-a63-brand or data-a63-surface alone. brand-action.css:14-15 re-declares only the primary action on [data-a63-brand]. --a63-text-accent (semantics.css:161,360), --a63-focus-ring (:209,395), --a63-selected-accent-background (:301,445), --a63-choice-card-checked-* (:199-205,388-393) and the surfaces and borders that read --surface-light/dark-* and --a63-brand-* (:100-185, :307-379) are declared only on ':root, .light, [data-a63-mode]' and ':is(.dark,[data-a63-mode=dark])', so they resolve at the ancestor and inherit frozen values. personalization-axes.md:4 promises 'applied at any scope'; :71 wrongly places --a63-focus-ring in brand.css on [data-a63-brand]. The nested-scope tests stamp theme and mode together (contrast.browser.test.ts:189-191), and the brand tests use the root only (:237). Stories always pass mode with brand (button.stories.tsx:692, switch.stories.tsx:327), which hides the bug.
findings.fix: Add [data-a63-brand] and [data-a63-surface] to the selector lists of both mode blocks of semantics.css, keyed to the inherited mode. The simplest form is to generate the light block as ':root, .light, [data-a63-mode=light], :not(.dark,[data-a63-mode=dark]) > [data-a63-brand]...'; a cleaner one moves the mode choice into a --a63-mode-is-dark switch and declares the brand- and surface-derived tokens on ':root, [data-a63-brand], [data-a63-surface], [data-a63-mode], .light, .dark' using light-dark() or a 0/1 mix. Then add a nested brand-only and surface-only case to contrast.browser.test.ts and correct personalization-axes.md:71.

findings.subject: Personalization axes (brand, surface, surface tint, radius, type scale, density, font, mode)
findings.summary: On a nested scope, the radius and type-scale axes do nothing, although the source comments say a subtree can override them.
findings.evidence: foundation/radius.css:16-32 and foundation/typography.css:18-49 declare the derived ramps at :root only; [data-a63-radius] and [data-a63-type-scale] change only the multiplier (radius.css:21-39, type-scale.css:12-26). radius.css:14 and type-scale.css:9-10 claim a subtree can reset them. story-probes.tsx:108-131 documents the freeze and re-emits the ramp inline as a workaround, and autocomplete.stories.tsx:220-235 ('Flush square items') sets data-a63-radius='none' on a wrapper that still draws var(--radius-lg) from the root. The test helpers set axes on documentElement only (test/apply-styles.ts:6-8).
findings.fix: Re-declare the --radius-* ramp on [data-a63-radius] and the --typography-* steps on [data-a63-type-scale] (as environment.css already does for density), move the story-probes workaround into the CSS, and add nested-scope cases to personalization-axes.browser.test.ts.

findings.subject: Theme: aqua
findings.summary: In a nested mode or theme-only scope, aqua loses its mode-split surfaces; terminal re-asserts its palette for descendants, but aqua does not.
findings.evidence: aqua.css:112 '[data-a63-theme=aqua]:is(:root,.light,[data-a63-mode=light])' and :134 '...:is(.dark,[data-a63-mode=dark])' have no descendant form, unlike terminal.css:94,152. A nested <UIProvider mode="dark"> re-runs semantics.css:306-326 and paints neutral modern-dark surfaces inside aqua. <UIProvider theme="aqua"> under an html-class mode matches neither rule.
findings.fix: Generate the descendant re-assertion for aqua (and modern.css:47) the same way as terminal: '[data-a63-theme=aqua] :is(.dark,[data-a63-mode=dark])', and a ':not(...)' or descendant light form. Add theme-only and nested-mode-inside-theme cases to the contrast test.

findings.subject: Theme: terminal
findings.summary: <UIProvider theme="terminal"> without a mode on the same element gets the CRT glow but neutral text and surfaces, and phosphor text ignores a nested brand.
findings.evidence: terminal.css:93-94 and 151-152 match only when the mode sits on the theme element or a descendant, never an ancestor (the next-themes html-class pattern). Phosphor text is color-mix(var(--a63-action-primary)) computed on the theme element (terminal.css:96-99, 154-158), so it freezes against a nested [data-a63-brand]. Not covered: contrast.browser.test.ts:189-191 always stamps theme and mode together.
findings.fix: Have UIProvider stamp the resolved mode whenever it stamps a theme, or add ':is(.dark,[data-a63-mode=dark]) [data-a63-theme=terminal]' ancestor forms. Declare the brand-derived phosphor tokens on [data-a63-brand] inside terminal too (same fix family as r2-tokens-1).

findings.subject: Foundation and semantic tokens (packages/styles/src/tokens)
findings.summary: --a63-status-*-foreground is not re-declared in the dark block, so a solid info or danger fill in a nested dark scope gets near-white text at 3.39:1 and 3.85:1. The pair is not declared in the contrast test.
findings.evidence: semantics.css:234-264 compute -foreground from var(--a63-status-*) in the light block only; the dark block :404-415 re-declares status-* and -subtle but not -foreground. Under a light root, -foreground keeps the step-600 result (white), while the nested fill is step 500: white on info-500 rgb(78,134,239) = 3.39:1, on danger-500 rgb(231,67,64) = 3.85:1. It reaches consumers as text-info-foreground (tailwind/theme.css:366) and --info-foreground (compat/shadcn.css:46). contrast.browser.test.ts:12-57 has no status-foreground-on-status-fill pair.
findings.fix: Re-declare the four -foreground tokens in the dark block (the generator already does this for -subtle), and add '{fg: --a63-status-X-foreground, bg: --a63-status-X, min: 4.5}' for each status to actionPairs, which also run nested.

findings.subject: Foundation and semantic tokens (packages/styles/src/tokens)
findings.summary: Chart series 2 and 3 are under 3:1 against the light page, and no chart or category pair is declared.
findings.evidence: semantics.css:270-271 set --a63-chart-2 to teal-500 and --a63-chart-3 to amber-500 on light surfaces (palette.css:43,98). Against the n1 light page rgb(249,249,249), teal-500 is about 2.3:1 and amber-500 about 2.0:1 (computed from the sRGB equivalents). The same 500 steps feed --a63-category-* (semantics.css:49-92), which AGENTS.md rule 9 steers chart series to. contrast.browser.test.ts declares no chart or category pair.
findings.fix: Either move the light-mode chart and category hues to step 600 or 700 where needed to reach 3:1 against the page and panel, and declare them as AA_UI pairs, or document that series need a direct label or outline (and enforce that in the chart recipe). Product direction on palette brightness may need YZ.

findings.subject: Foundation and semantic tokens (packages/styles/src/tokens)
findings.summary: Dead tokens are not checked. The token-economy unused scan only covers prefixes that no longer exist, and 60 --a63-* tokens in packages/styles have no reader in the repo.
findings.evidence: check-token-economy.mjs:42-46 filters with /^--(theme|gel)-/; there are 0 such declarations in packages/styles/src, so the log always says '0 unused'. A multiline-aware scan of packages/ and apps/ finds 60 unread --a63-* tokens, including 40 --a63-badge-<hue>-accent/-foreground (contracts/badge.css:10-53; the Badge recipe reads --badge-bg/--badge-fg), --a63-status-danger-subtle(-foreground) (semantics.css:265-266), --a63-choice-thumb, --a63-choice-feedback-duration, --a63-toggle-group-gap, --a63-toggle-shadow-active, --a63-trigger-indicator-size, --a63-action-control-gap, and the weather border, divider, muted-foreground and text-shadow tokens that three themes set (aqua.css, retro.css, terminal.css) but no web recipe reads.
findings.fix: Scan --a63-* and the theme-private prefixes in use (--aqua-, --retro-, --terminal-) for unused tokens, fail on new ones against a baseline, then delete or wire up the listed tokens. If the weather tokens serve an app outside this repo, say so in the contract.

findings.subject: Foundation and semantic tokens (packages/styles/src/tokens)
findings.summary: The type scale is not monotonic: 10xl (the display role) is a fixed 40px, below 9xl's 44px at 640px and 49px at 768px. The steps around it are a 1px step and then a 1.4x jump.
findings.evidence: foundation/typography.css:47-48 (10xl 40/44, 11xl 56/60, with no breakpoint override) against :53-98 (9xl 44px at >=40rem, 49px at >=48rem). type-roles.css:27 maps --a63-type-display-font-size to 10xl, so 'display' renders smaller than the 9xl step on tablet and desktop. At the base width, 9xl to 10xl is 39 to 40px.
findings.fix: Give 10xl and 11xl breakpoint steps that stay above 9xl (or renumber so the display steps sit above the responsive ramp), and add a test that every step is at least the one below it at each window size.

findings.subject: Tailwind bridge (packages/styles/src/tailwind)
findings.summary: Density does not reach Tailwind spacing utilities, so compact density tightens the components but not the p-*, gap-* and m-* layout the templates are built with.
findings.evidence: tailwind/theme.css defines no --spacing (grep finds no 'spacing' in the file); Tailwind's default 0.25rem unit applies. --a63-space-unit is the density-scaled unit (space.css:18; density.browser.test.ts:41-44). Templates lay out with utilities such as 'flex flex-col gap-6 p-6' (app-view template), and the template description tells builders to use <UIProvider density="compact"> for dense views.
findings.fix: Map Tailwind's --spacing to var(--a63-space-unit) in @theme inline (or document that layout utilities are density-invariant and give templates density-aware gap tokens). Check that the change is intended across the templates' visual baselines.

findings.subject: Tailwind bridge (packages/styles/src/tailwind)
findings.summary: The bridge keeps Tailwind's names with other values: text-6xl is 28px rather than 60px, text-9xl is 39-49px, and rounded-full (a pill) and --radius-full (a 28px corner) are one name with two meanings.
findings.evidence: foundation/typography.css:39,45 (6xl 28px, 9xl 39px) exposed as --text-6xl/--text-9xl in tailwind/theme.css; theme.css:517-519 maps rounded-full to --radius-pill while foundation/radius.css:32 keeps --radius-full = 2 x xl. A builder or agent fluent in Tailwind gets a different result for the same class.
findings.fix: Decide between keeping Tailwind's numeric meaning (and moving the DS ramp to role utilities such as text-title-1, which type-roles already provides) and documenting the remap prominently in atom63 rules and docs. Rename --radius-full (for example --radius-soft) so that 'full' means a pill everywhere.

findings.subject: shadcn bridges (compat/shadcn.css, compat/a63-from-shadcn.css)
findings.summary: shadcn aliases are declared only on mode scopes, so inside a brand-, theme- or surface-only UIProvider, --primary, --ring and --background disagree with the --a63-* tokens.
findings.evidence: compat/shadcn.css:14-17 '(:root, .light, .dark, [data-a63-mode])'; brand-action.css:14-15 changes --a63-action-primary on [data-a63-brand]; provider.tsx:68,73,74 stamp brand, surface and theme alone.
findings.fix: Generate the alias block on ':root, .light, .dark, [data-a63-mode], [data-a63-brand], [data-a63-theme], [data-a63-surface]' (generate-role-bridges.mjs), together with r2-tokens-1.

findings.subject: shadcn bridges (compat/shadcn.css, compat/a63-from-shadcn.css)
findings.summary: The reverse bridge hard-codes white foregrounds on the status fills, about 2:1 on its own warning fallback, and no test covers it.
findings.evidence: a63-from-shadcn.css:40-45: --a63-status-warning: var(--warning, oklch(0.75 0.15 80)) with --a63-status-warning-foreground: white, and success oklch(0.65 0.16 150) with white. a63-from-shadcn.css:15 declares only on :root.
findings.fix: Use the same auto-contrast expression as semantics.css:250-252 (oklch(from var(--a63-status-warning) clamp(...))) for the four status foregrounds, and add a small contrast test that loads only the reverse bridge with a stock shadcn palette.

findings.subject: Theme authoring (adding a theme)
findings.summary: Adding a theme touches about ten hand-written lists that the docs do not name and no check guards, unlike brands.
findings.evidence: theme-authoring.md:58-75 names the resolver and check-theme-authoring.mjs only. Theme ids are also hard-coded in themes/index.css:1-4, ui-foundation/src/axes.ts, ui-react/src/theme/core/types.ts and options.ts, styles/scripts/generate-figma-sync.mjs, contrast.browser.test.ts:9, figma-parity.browser.test.ts:145,150, check-theme-authoring.mjs:15-21 and story-probes (THEME_RADIUS_SCALE). check-theme-authoring.mjs:55 runs brandListProblems for brands only.
findings.fix: Add a themeListProblems check that compares each list with the themes/*.resolver.json files (mirroring lib/brand-lists.mjs), derive the test and check lists from that source, and list the remaining manual edits in theme-authoring.md.

findings.subject: Theme: terminal
findings.summary: In Figma, terminal's brand-tracking phosphor colors always show the b1 value, and the parity test leaves these 'computed' tokens out.
findings.evidence: atom63.figma-sync.json 'computed' lists --a63-text-primary, -secondary, -tertiary, --a63-border-*, --a63-surface-page/-panel and --a63-action-neutral* with variesOn [brand, mode, surface, theme]; terminal.css:96-170 mixes them from --a63-action-primary. figma-parity.browser.test.ts:15-19,134 excludes computed tokens.
findings.fix: Emit terminal's brand-derived colors as a Theme x Brand product collection (or per-brand terminal modes) in generate-figma-sync.mjs, or alias them to Brand-collection variables so that switching the Brand mode re-tints them. Then drop them from 'computed'.

findings.subject: Figma sync and parity (generated/atom63.figma-sync.json)
findings.summary: Figma has no phone form-factor, compact-density control geometry or coarse-pointer sizes, so designs drawn for those contexts use comfortable desktop values.
findings.evidence: Model 'skipped' tally: 60 "context scope: [data-a63-form-factor='phone']...", 32 ':is([data-a63-density], [data-density])', 53 'conditional' (@media pointer: coarse, prefers-reduced-motion, max-width). --a63-control-height-xs..xl are in 'computed'. The Density collection holds only the --a63-space-* steps.
findings.fix: Add a Form Factor collection (desktop, phone) and move the density-scoped control tokens into the Density collection as concrete per-mode values (the generator already resolves values per context in the browser). Keep 'conditional' tokens out only where Figma has no equivalent.

findings.subject: Personalization axes (brand, surface, surface tint, radius, type scale, density, font, mode)
findings.summary: UIProvider mode="system" stamps light whatever the OS preference, so 'system', a documented value of the mode axis, never resolves to dark on a nested scope.
findings.evidence: ui-react/src/provider.tsx:65 'const resolvedMode = mode === 'system' ? 'light' : mode', stamped at :72. personalization-axes.md:22 lists system as a mode value. applyPersonalization resolves system with matchMedia (apply-personalization.ts:3-14), so the two stamping paths disagree.
findings.fix: Resolve 'system' in UIProvider with useSyncExternalStore over matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') (light on the server), or leave data-a63-mode unset and add a prefers-color-scheme fallback block in semantics.css.

findings.subject: Foundation and semantic tokens (packages/styles/src/tokens)
findings.summary: There is no inverse-surface token. Six recipe sites paint --a63-text-primary as a fill or --a63-surface-page as text, and they sit in the craft baseline.
findings.evidence: craft-baseline.json token-role entries: card.css (2), input-otp.css, slider.css, kbd.css, mdx timeline.css.
findings.fix: Add --a63-surface-inverse and --a63-text-inverse (aliases of the current values, with a declared 4.5:1 pair), move the six sites onto them, and empty the token-role baseline.

findings.subject: Foundation and semantic tokens (packages/styles/src/tokens)
findings.summary: Component-tier tokens sit in the semantic layer, two semantic surfaces duplicate each other, and the shadcn bridge adds generic global names.
findings.evidence: semantics.css:187-205 (--a63-control-outline-*, --a63-alert-background, --a63-choice-card-checked-*); --a63-surface-sidebar equals --a63-surface-recessed in both modes (semantics.css:142-144, 345-346); compat/shadcn.css:166-167 '--light' and '--dark'.
findings.fix: Move the component tokens to their contracts (contracts/action.css, alert, choice), alias recessed to sidebar or merge them, and rename --light/--dark to --a63-fixed-light/-dark in the bridge.

findings.subject: Personalization axes (brand, surface, surface tint, radius, type scale, density, font, mode)
findings.summary: Legacy attribute aliases (data-density, data-input) and a stale radius comment remain.
findings.evidence: token-economy.log selectors ':is([data-a63-density], [data-density])' and ':is([data-a63-input='touch'], [data-input='touch'])'; density.browser.test.ts:77-78 tests the legacy name. foundation/radius.css:29 says '2× md' while :32 is 2× xl.
findings.fix: Set a removal date for the legacy names (warn in UIProvider or the docs), and fix the comment in radius.tokens.json and regenerate.

findings.subject: Theme: modern
findings.summary: Modern's dark-only widget face has no descendant form, so a nested dark scope inside a light modern root drops it.
findings.evidence: modern.css:47-51 '[data-a63-theme=modern]:is(.dark,[data-a63-mode=dark])' with no '[data-a63-theme=modern] :is(.dark,...)' form.
findings.fix: Generate the descendant form together with r2-tokens-3.
